page: Amazon Web Services r6g.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors. It operates on an arm64 architecture featuring a single dedicated physical core and vCPU based on the ARM Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache, running under the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

The hardware configuration provides 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio characteristic of AWS memory-optimized tiers. There are no discrete hardware accelerators, with a GPU count of zero. Additionally, the instance contains no local NVMe storage and relies entirely on networked Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk storage, with a baseline network bandwidth specification of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the single-core execution boundary of the platform. Single-core compute stress tests deliver mid-tier results with a stress-ng metric of 1491.89, whereas multi-core and aggregate throughput scores rank lower relative to larger multi-threaded instances. Geekbench delivers 948.0 in single-core and 946.0 in multi-core routines. Memory read bandwidth reaches 59.31 GB/s for small cached blocks and 19.58 GB/s for 256 MB uncached transfers, supporting up to 1.17 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

Resource allocation provides cost efficiency for low-scale operations that require a higher memory-to-core balance without paying for unnecessary multi-core capacity. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and limited network baseline bandwidth represent key operational constraints. AWS r6g.medium is best aligned with low-throughput in-memory caching nodes, lightweight Redis or Memcached instances, microservice background tasks, and small development databases requiring an 8 GB footprint.
